content:
Apple has finally responded to the sharply rising costs of memory and other components, and it is pulling no punches. Some of the price hikes exceed 50%, and upgrades to memory and storage have in some cases doubled outright.

These higher prices are very likely to persist for years, and may never come back down...

9to5Mac readers were already skeptical that Apple would drop prices once component shortages eased. More than two-thirds of respondents expected the price increases to be permanent.

A subsequent analyst report noted that supply chain pricing will not improve in any meaningful way before 2028, and even then any relief would be modest. Pricing well above historical levels will be in place for at least several years, and quite possibly forever.

If that turns out to be the case, how will you respond? Will you grit your teeth and keep buying Apple products at the same pace? Will you cut back on how many Apple products you buy, or how often? Or will you take other steps, like buying lower-tier models, opting for refurbished units, or waiting for sales?

Feel free to take our poll and share your thoughts in the comments. The poll allows multiple selections in case you plan to change your spending habits in more than one way.
